title: Tuga WH6 vs Tuga W8: Windows Handheld or 8 Inch Tablet?
description: Tuga WH6 (Windows handheld, £699) or Tuga W8 (8 inch Windows tablet, £629)? £70 apart, both IP65 and MIL-STD-810H. Which to buy, and when the cheaper W8 wins.
summary: £70 apart, both IP65, MIL-STD-810H and with removable batteries: the WH6 is a 470g handheld that fits a holster; the W8 is an 8 inch tablet with a newer Intel N150, a Full HD 550 nit screen, mini HDMI and a bigger battery.
lede: For anyone who needs Windows on site and is torn between a handheld and an 8 inch tablet. The short answer: buy the Tuga W8 and keep £70 if the work happens on the screen, and pay the extra for the Tuga WH6 only if the device has to live in a holster or a pocket all day.
verdict: Shape decides this one. The Tuga WH6 costs £699 and the Tuga W8 costs £629, so the handheld is £70 more. Both run Windows 11 with 8GB of RAM and 128GB of eMMC storage, both are sealed to IP65 and tested to MIL-STD-810H, both are rated to work from -20°C to 60°C, and both have a removable battery, 4G LTE, NFC, GPS, a microSD slot, USB-C and USB-A. The extra £70 does not buy more computer: the W8 has the newer Intel N150 (up to 3.6GHz) against the WH6's Intel Celeron N5100 (up to 2.8GHz). It buys a 6.5 inch device at 470g that fits a belt holster, a 1.5 metre drop rating against the W8's 1.22 metres, and 45W USB-C PD charging. If you spend the day on your feet, working one-handed, that is what you are paying for.

If the work happens on the screen, the W8 is the better buy as well as the cheaper one. Its 8 inch 1920 x 1200 display is the bigger, sharper and brighter of the two at 550 nits, against 400 nits on the WH6's 6.5 inch 720 x 1600 screen. That gives you more room for a form, a drawing or a spreadsheet. It has mini HDMI output for a monitor, Wi-Fi 6 against Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.2 against 5.0, and a 5000mAh battery against 4000mAh, removable on both. The cost is bulk: 818g against 470g, carried on a hand strap (one is in the box) or in a bag rather than a pocket.

Two things to know before you order either. The WH6 runs Windows 11 IoT and the W8 Windows 11 Pro, so if a software provider specifies an edition, ask them which they support, and in both cases check that the programs you rely on run on the device rather than assuming they will. Both have scanner versions that read 2D codes such as QR, Data Matrix and PDF417: the WH6 with Barcode Scanner is £779, £80 over the standard WH6, and the W8 with 2D Scanner is £699, £70 over the standard W8. For delivery and warehouse work, the logistics page covers why a handheld suits the job; for engineers whose diagnostic software only runs on Windows, the field service page covers the W8.
chooseA: The device lives in a holster or a pocket between tasks: the WH6 is a 6.5 inch handheld at 470g, 348g lighter than the W8.
You work one-handed all day, walking a site or scanning (a built-in scan engine needs the £779 scanner version), and you would rather not carry an 8 inch tablet on a hand strap.
You want the higher listed drop height: 1.5 metres on the WH6 against 1.22 metres on the W8, both alongside MIL-STD-810H.
You charge from USB-C: the WH6 lists 45W USB-C PD charging, where the W8 lists a 48W adapter.
You photograph labels and meter readings close up: the WH6's 8MP rear camera is listed as autofocus, and the W8's 8MP camera is not.
chooseB: The work happens on the screen: forms, drawings and desktop software are easier on 8 inches at 1920 x 1200 than on 6.5 inches at 720 x 1600, and you keep £70.
You read it outdoors: the W8 is rated at 550 nits against the WH6's 400.
You plug into a screen: the W8 has mini HDMI output alongside the USB-C and USB-A ports both devices have.
You want the newer processor and the bigger battery: an Intel N150 against a Celeron N5100, and 5000mAh against 4000mAh, both removable.

You want a locking vehicle mount or a tablet dock: the W8 fits the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) and the Charging Dock (£49.99), where the WH6 has the Car Phone Mount (£17) and the Charging Cradle (£79).

faq.q: Is the Tuga WH6 worth £70 more than the Tuga W8?
faq.a: Only if you need the shape. The WH6 costs £699 and the W8 £629, and they share 8GB of RAM, 128GB of storage, IP65, MIL-STD-810H, a removable battery, 4G LTE and NFC, so the £70 buys a smaller, lighter device, not more computer; the W8's Intel N150 is the newer processor. If the device spends its day in your hands while you read, or on a tablet dock or a vehicle mounting dock, the Tuga W8 gives you a bigger, sharper and brighter screen, HDMI, Wi-Fi 6 and a bigger battery for less. If it spends its day in a holster, the Tuga WH6 earns the difference. Both come with the same 12 month warranty, and the paid 3-Year Warranty is £89 on the WH6 and £79 on the W8. Both prices have no VAT to add, and delivery is free to UK addresses in 7 to 10 working days.

faq.q: Which one should I buy for barcode scanning?
faq.a: The Tuga WH6 with Barcode Scanner if scanning is the main job, the Tuga W8 with 2D Scanner if it is one part of a bigger task. Both come in a scanner version sold from the same product page as the standard model, and both read 2D codes such as QR, Data Matrix and PDF417: the WH6 version is £779, £80 over the standard WH6, and the W8 version is £699, £70 over the standard W8, so the two are £80 apart. For scanning as the main job, parcels, stock or assets all day, the handheld is the natural shape: the standard WH6 weighs 470g and has a Belt Holster (£22) listed for it, though the scanner version's weight is not listed. For scanning as part of a bigger task, a stock count that also needs a bigger screen, say, the W8 version does the scanning and gives you the screen for the rest. Our guide to built-in barcode scanners covers when the extra cost pays off at all.

faq.q: How do the batteries and charging compare?
faq.a: The W8 carries a 5000mAh battery and the WH6 4000mAh, so the tablet starts the day with a quarter more capacity. Both are removable, so either can take a charged spare; spare batteries are not listed with the accessories, so check with us before you count on swapping one. The WH6 lists 45W USB-C PD charging and the W8 a 48W adapter. For charging in place, the WH6 Charging Cradle is £79 and the Charging Dock for the W8 is £49.99, and the 12V DC Car Charger (£26) fits either (see accessories). Both are rated to work from -20°C to 60°C. Our guide to rugged tablets in winter explains what the cold does to either battery.

faq.q: Do they run the same Windows software?
faq.a: Not necessarily, so check. Both run Windows 11 with 8GB of RAM, but the processors and editions differ: an Intel Celeron N5100 and Windows 11 IoT on the WH6, an Intel N150 and Windows 11 Pro on the W8. Storage is 128GB of eMMC in both, with a microSD slot on each (the WH6 lists cards up to 512GB). If your software provider says which Windows editions they support, ask them about the one you are considering, and check that the specific programs you rely on run on the device before you order.
